name: CO2 to concrete and aggregates
principle: CO2 is injected into concrete during mixing, where it mineralises and raises compressive strength, allowing less cement. CarbonCure reports more than 500,000 t of CO2 saved over 7.5 million truckloads, with hundreds of systems in more than two dozen countries.

performance.metric: CO2 saved by CarbonCure to the date of the article
performance.basis: 7.5 million truckloads; date not stated in text read

source.note: gasworld, CarbonCure hits 500,000 tonnes CO2 milestone

performance.metric: CO2 mineralisation dose and embodied-carbon reduction in ready-mix concrete (CarbonCure)
performance.unit: % CO2 by weight of cement injected (0.1%), giving a 4-6% Global Warming Potential reduction per truck; each tonne mineralised avoids roughly 40 t CO2 via cement reduction (company figures)
performance.basis: CarbonCure technical note: CO2 is injected at a dose of 0.1% by weight of cement; Stevenson information sheet: concrete made with CarbonCure provides a 4-6% reduction to GWP; CarbonCure brochure: every tonne mineralised prevents roughly 40 t CO2 by reducing cement; milestone of 500,000 t CO2 saved across 7.5 million truckloads (Oct 2024)

source.note: CarbonCure Measuring CO2 Mineralization note (2023); Stevenson sheet; carbonherald 28 Oct 2024; read 2026-10-28
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'CO2 sequestration in inert carbonate materials (mineralisation)' 9 (2025)

limitations: Per-batch CO2 amount is small; cement saving not quantified in the article
